_aprasas: Brėžly lessons in English. Overlay on pamokos.json by lesson and step id: only the texts. Ids, XP, checks and correct test answers (t) come from pamokos.json.

failas.aprasas: A new drawing from acadiso.dwt, units, saving as DWG and PDF - every job starts here.
failas.pabaiga: You can start a drawing correctly and save it as DWG and PDF.

naujas.kodel: acadiso.dwt is the metric template: everything in millimetres. acad.dwt uses inches, so the dimensions in your drawing would be wrong.
zingsniai: Top left, click A (Application) → New → Drawing.
Pick acadiso.dwt in the list → Open.
uzuominos: If it opens without a dialog, type STARTUP → 0 and try again.
The template folder opens automatically - look for acadiso.dwt, not acad.dwt.

vienetai.kodel: Units say what the number 100 means. In our drawings it is 100 millimetres, with no unnecessary decimals.
zingsniai: Type UNITS and set:
uzuominos: Precision 0 means whole numbers - enough for these drawings.

dwg.kodel: DWG is AutoCAD's native format. A meaningful file name helps you find your work a week later.
zingsniai: Press Ctrl+Shift+S (SAVEAS).
Choose a folder, type the name My_first_part → Save.
uzuominos: For an older AutoCAD (e.g. at school) choose AutoCAD 2013 Drawing.
Later, Ctrl+S simply saves your changes.

pdf.kodel: Assignments are often handed in as PDF. The DWG To PDF printer creates a file instead of paper.
zingsniai: Type PLOT (or Ctrl+P).
Printer: DWG To PDF.pc3, Plot area: Extents, Fit to paper → OK → Save.
uzuominos: Save the PDF in the same folder as the DWG - easier to find.
If the PDF is empty, the drawing has nothing in it yet - that's fine at this step.

testas.k: Which template should you use for drawings in millimetres?
testas.p: acadiso.dwt is metric (ISO). acad.dwt uses inches.

testas.k: What is the DXF format used for?
v: Opening a drawing in other CAD programs
testas.p: DXF is an exchange format that most CAD programs can open.

testas.k: An old AutoCAD at school won't open your file. What do you do?
v: SAVEAS → an older DWG version, e.g. 2013
testas.p: Newer DWG versions don't open in older programs - save in an older format.

kampinis-irasas.aprasas: Your first drawing: a 185 × 40 title block table with RECTANG, LINE and TEXT. In the last lesson you will move it onto an A3 sheet.
kampinis-irasas.pabaiga: You drew your first drawing - the title block table. In the last lesson it will land in the corner of an A3 sheet.

ki-konturas.kodel: The title block is the drawing's „passport“: who drew it, who checked it, the scale. It is a 185 × 40 mm table. You enter points as x,y coordinates: the first number goes right, the second goes up.
zingsniai: In Model space type RECTANG and two opposite corners of the rectangle:
uzuominos: Why not 0,0? This is the bottom right corner of an A3 sheet - in the last lesson the table will land in its place.
Can't see the table? Type ZOOM → E (Extents).

ki-linijos.kodel: The lines split the table into cells: on the left - Drawn, Checked, Date; on the right - the drawing title, scale and sheet.
zingsniai: First - the vertical divider:
The other lines the same way, each with its own LINE command.
Right: 295,20 → 415,20, and below it the verticals 335,5 → 335,20 and 375,5 → 375,20.
uzuominos: Enter ends LINE, one more Enter starts a new line.
Turn on OSNAP (F3) - the mouse will snap exactly to corners.
Made a mistake? Ctrl+Z undoes the last action.

ki-tekstas.kodel: An empty title block is the first thing your tutor will notice.
zingsniai: Top right: the drawing title (height 5); on the left, in the „Drawn“ row - your name (height 2.5).
uzuominos: Enter twice ends the TEXT command.
You can move text with MOVE.
You will learn proper ISO fonts in the lesson „Fonts and text“.
ki-tekstas.tikslas: At least 2 texts in the table

ki-issaugok.kodel: You will use this table in the last lesson - you will copy it into the corner of an A3 sheet.
zingsniai: Press Ctrl+Shift+S (SAVEAS), type the name Title_block → Save.
uzuominos: Avoid special letters in file names - some programs don't understand them.

testas.k: What size is the title block in these drawings?
testas.p: The title block is 185 × 40 mm, in the bottom right corner of the border.

testas.k: What does the coordinate 230,5 mean?
testas.p: The first number is x (right), the second is y (up).

testas.k: How do you end the LINE command?
testas.p: Enter (or Esc) ends the command, one more Enter repeats it.

tikslumas.aprasas: Navigation (ZOOM, PAN), object snap (OSNAP), tracking (OTRACK, POLAR) and measuring (AREA) - you'll draw precisely, not by eye.
tikslumas.pabaiga: Now you draw precisely: snaps, tracking, polar angles and measuring - the basis for every other drawing.

tk-naujas.kodel: The drawing is big and the screen is small - you need to zoom, pan and see everything quickly. The mouse wheel is all it takes.
zingsniai: NEW → acadiso.dwt (millimetres).
Roll the mouse wheel - the view zooms towards the cursor.
Hold the wheel down and drag - the view pans (PAN).
Double-click the wheel - you'll see the whole drawing (ZOOM Extents). Same as Z → E.
komandos: Specify corner of window or [All/Center/Dynamic/Extents/Previous/Scale/Window/Object] <real time>:
uzuominos: Lost in the drawing? Double-click the wheel and you see everything again.
The wheel zooms too much? Just roll it back.

tk-osnap.kodel: Without snaps a click lands only „roughly“. With OSNAP the cursor sticks exactly to an endpoint, midpoint or centre - the most important precision tool.
zingsniai: Type OSNAP - the Drafting Settings window opens.
On the Object Snap tab tick: Endpoint, Midpoint, Center, Quadrant, Intersection.
Object Snap On (F3) must be ticked at the top → OK.
uzuominos: Don't tick every snap - too many markers just get in the way. These five are enough.
F3 turns snapping on and off. The cursor stopped snapping? Press F3.

tk-rombas.kodel: You can't find the middle of an edge exactly by eye. The Midpoint snap finds it for you - hover over the line and a triangle appears.
zingsniai: Draw an 80 × 50 rectangle.
LINE and click the midpoint of the bottom edge (a triangle ▲ appears), then the midpoints of the right, top and left edges.
Finish with C (Close) - the line returns to the start.
uzuominos: No triangle? Check that F3 is on and Midpoint is ticked.
The rhombus corners: 40,0 · 80,25 · 40,50 · 0,25.
tk-rombas.tikslas: An 80 × 50 rectangle and a rhombus through the edge midpoints

tk-centras.kodel: Sometimes a point isn't marked anywhere - like the centre of the rhombus. Object snap tracking (OTRACK) draws dotted lines from other points, and where they cross is the point you need.
zingsniai: Turn tracking on: F11 (Object Snap Tracking lights up at the bottom).
CIRCLE. Hover over the midpoint of the top edge and wait a second (don't click!) - a small plus appears.
Do the same with the midpoint of the left edge, then move the cursor to the middle of the rectangle - two dotted lines cross. Click.
Radius 10.
uzuominos: No dotted lines? Press F11 and hover over the midpoint a little longer.
The centre must be 40,25. Try it with tracking - coordinates aren't always known.
tk-centras.tikslas: An R10 circle in the centre of the rhombus

tk-polar.kodel: ORTHO (F8) only lets you draw horizontally and vertically, while POLAR (F10) works at a chosen angle, e.g. every 30°. Point the cursor, type the length - and the line is exact.
zingsniai: Right-click the POLAR button at the bottom → choose 30. Turn on F10.
LINE and click the top right corner of the rectangle (Endpoint).
Move the cursor up and to the right until a dotted line and 30° appear. Type 40 → Enter → Enter.
uzuominos: You type only the number and the cursor gives the direction - this is „direct distance entry“.
The same without tracking: @40<30.
tk-polar.tikslas: A 40 mm line at 30° from corner 80,50

tk-plotas.kodel: You often need a length or an area - e.g. for the amount of material. AutoCAD measures exactly: DIST - a distance, AREA - an area.
zingsniai: AREA and click the 4 corners of the rhombus (Endpoint) → Enter.
The command line shows Area = ... Write that number with TEXT next to the rectangle, e.g. A = ... (height 3.5).
uzuominos: The area of the rhombus is half the area of the rectangle.
DIST measures the distance between two points - check the 30° line: it must be 40.
tk-plotas.tikslas: A text with the rhombus area

testas.k: What does F3 do?
v: Turns object snap (OSNAP) on and off
testas.p: F3 - OSNAP, F8 - ORTHO, F10 - POLAR, F11 - OTRACK.

testas.k: How do you quickly see the whole drawing?
testas.p: Double-clicking the wheel or Z → E shows all objects in the drawing.

testas.k: With POLAR 30° you point the cursor along 30° and type 40. What is drawn?
testas.p: When you type only a number, the line goes in the cursor direction with that length.

2d.aprasas: Layers, RECTANG, CIRCLE, centre lines and FILLET - you will draw a plate with holes.
2d.pabaiga: You drew a 2D plate with holes, centre lines and rounded corners.

sluoksniai2d.kodel: Outline, centre lines and dimensions go on different layers with different line types, as the standard requires.
zingsniai: LAYER → New Layer: KONTURAS (outline, colour 7), ASYS (centre lines, colour 1, linetype CENTER), MATMENYS (dimensions, colour 3).
Double-click KONTURAS - it becomes current.
uzuominos: Load the CENTER linetype via Load...
The colour number is shown at the bottom of the dialog.

plokste.kodel: We start at 0,0 - the easiest way to work out the other coordinates.
zingsniai: On layer KONTURAS type:
uzuominos: Type coordinates with a comma and no spaces.
Double-click the mouse wheel to see the whole drawing.

centras.kodel: The centre hole is ø30. CIRCLE asks for the radius, so we enter half the diameter - 15.
zingsniai: Type:
uzuominos: To enter the diameter instead, press D and type 30.

skyles.kodel: Holes ø10 in the corners, 15 mm from the edges.
zingsniai: Draw 4 circles with radius 5:
uzuominos: An empty Enter (or Space) repeats the last command.
You can draw one and copy it with COPY.

asys.kodel: Centre lines show symmetry and hole centres. They are thin dash-dot lines that extend beyond the outline.
zingsniai: Make layer ASYS current and draw two lines:
uzuominos: If the line looks continuous - LTSCALE → 0.5.
Centre lines extend 5 mm beyond the outline.

fillet.kodel: Sharp corners are dangerous and look bad. FILLET with the Polyline option rounds all 4 corners at once.
zingsniai: On layer KONTURAS type:
uzuominos: Only one corner rounded? You forgot P (Polyline). Undo: U.
Radius 10 - corners rounded R10.

testas.k: Which number do you enter in CIRCLE for a ø30 hole?
testas.p: CIRCLE asks for the radius - half the diameter.

testas.k: Which layer are centre lines drawn on?
testas.p: Centre lines go on their own layer with the CENTER linetype.

testas.k: How do you round all corners of a rectangle with FILLET at once?
testas.p: The Polyline option rounds every corner of the polyline.

redagavimas.aprasas: A plate with two slots: chamfers (CHAMFER), a copy (COPY), tangent lines (Quadrant), trimming (TRIM) and a mirror image (MIRROR).
redagavimas.pabaiga: You can edit now: copy, chamfer, trim and mirror. Most real parts are drawn like this - not from scratch, but from what is already there.

rd-sluoksniai.kodel: Every job gets a new drawing with the same layers. Engineers do the same: they start from a template.
zingsniai: NEW → acadiso.dwt.
LAYER → create KONTURAS (7), ASYS (1, linetype CENTER), MATMENYS (3) - as in the lesson „2D drawing“.
Make KONTURAS current.
uzuominos: Tip: save such an empty drawing as a template (SAVEAS → AutoCAD Drawing Template .dwt) - next time you won't need to create the layers.
Never draw on layer 0 - it's meant for blocks.

rd-plokste.kodel: The base is a rectangle. The next steps will edit it, not draw it again.
zingsniai: On layer KONTURAS:
uzuominos: @ means „from the last point“: @120,80 - 120 to the right and 80 up.

rd-chamfer.kodel: A chamfer is a cut-off corner - like FILLET, but straight. D (Distance) sets how much to cut, P (Polyline) chamfers all corners at once.
zingsniai: Type:
uzuominos: Only one corner chamfered? You forgot P (Polyline). U and again.
On a drawing this chamfer is written 10×45°.

rd-kopija.pavadinimas: Start of the slot: CIRCLE and COPY
rd-kopija.kodel: When you need a second identical object, don't draw it again. COPY: select, give a base point and where to put it. MOVE works exactly the same, it just doesn't leave the original.
zingsniai: An R6 circle at 25,40.
COPY: select it → Enter → base point - the centre → @30,0 → Enter.
uzuominos: You can also select before the command: click the object, then COPY.
To snap to the centre, hover over the circle line - the centre marker appears.

rd-liestines.kodel: A slot is two half-circles and two straight lines across their top and bottom. The Quadrant snap finds the exact top and bottom points of a circle.
zingsniai: LINE → type QUA → click the top of the left circle → QUA → the top of the right circle → Enter.
The same at the bottom.
uzuominos: QUA is a one-off snap, it works for the next click only. The same: Shift + right mouse button → Quadrant.
rd-liestines.tikslas: Two tangent lines: y = 46 and y = 34

rd-trim.kodel: TRIM cuts off part of an object up to other objects. The inner halves of the circles aren't needed - trim them and a real slot remains.
zingsniai: TRIM → click the right half of the left circle (between the lines) and the left half of the right circle → Enter.
komandos: Select object to trim or shift-select to extend:
Select object to trim or shift-select to extend:
Select object to trim or shift-select to extend:
uzuominos: In recent AutoCAD TRIM cuts to the nearest lines by itself - just click what to cut off.
Trimmed the wrong part? U undoes the last trim without ending the command.
Hold Shift and TRIM extends a line to a boundary (like EXTEND).

rd-mirror.kodel: Half of a symmetric part is drawn and the other half is mirrored. The mirror line goes through the middle of the plate, and a selection box helps you select.
zingsniai: MIRROR. Select the slot with a box from left to right (blue): click left above the slot, then right below it → Enter.
Mirror line: top edge midpoint → bottom edge midpoint (Midpoint).
Erase source objects? → N.
komandos: (a box from left to right around the slot)
Specify first point of mirror line:
Specify second point of mirror line:
uzuominos: A box from left to right (blue) selects only what fits inside it completely. From right to left (green) - everything it touches.
The mirror line is x = 60 - the middle of the plate.

testas.k: A 10×45° chamfer: which distances do you enter in CHAMFER?
testas.p: A 45° angle comes from two equal distances.

testas.k: How is COPY different from MOVE?
v: COPY leaves the original, MOVE doesn't
testas.p: Both ask for a base point and where to put it, but COPY leaves the original in place.

testas.k: A box from left to right (blue) selects...
v: only objects that fit inside the box completely
testas.p: A box from right to left (green) also selects what it only touches.

masyvai.aprasas: A flange with 6 holes: a parallel copy (OFFSET), changing a layer, a polar array (ARRAYPOLAR), rotation (ROTATE) and centre lines.
masyvai.pabaiga: You drew a flange: OFFSET, changing a layer, a polar array and rotation. Arrays save the most time - 6 or 60 holes take the same effort.

ms-sluoksniai.kodel: A new job - a new drawing. If you saved a template with layers, start from it.
zingsniai: NEW → acadiso.dwt (or your template).
Layers KONTURAS (7), ASYS (1, CENTER), MATMENYS (3); KONTURAS current.
uzuominos: Already have a template with layers? NEW → pick it - the layers will be there.

ms-offset.kodel: OFFSET draws a parallel copy at a given distance - for a line, circle or polyline. For a circle it is a concentric circle.
zingsniai: A ⌀100 circle: CIRCLE → 0,0 → 50.
OFFSET → 30 → click the circle → click inside it → Enter. You get a ⌀40 bore.
komandos: Specify point on side to offset:
uzuominos: The distance is taken off the radius: 50 − 30 = 20, so you get R20 (⌀40).
OFFSET stays on - you can copy again at the same distance.

ms-pcd.kodel: Hole centres are marked with a thin centre line - the pitch circle. You'll draw it with OFFSET and move it to layer ASYS: this is how you change the layer of any object.
zingsniai: OFFSET → 15 → click the ⌀100 circle → click inside → Enter. You get ⌀70.
Click the new circle without any command - it gets selected.
Pick ASYS in the Home → Layers list → Esc.
komandos: Specify point on side to offset:
uzuominos: Another way: select the object and press Ctrl+1 - in Properties set Layer → ASYS.
MATCHPROP (MA) copies the layer and other properties from one object to others.
ms-pcd.tikslas: A ⌀70 pitch circle on layer ASYS

ms-skyle.kodel: The first hole sits at the top of the pitch circle. The array will create the other five.
zingsniai: Check that KONTURAS is current.
CIRCLE → click the top of the ⌀70 circle (Quadrant ◇) → 5.
uzuominos: The centre must be 0,35.
The hole ended up on layer ASYS? Select it and pick KONTURAS.

ms-masyvas.kodel: A polar array spaces copies evenly around a centre. You give the centre and the count - AutoCAD works out the angles.
zingsniai: ARRAYPOLAR → click the hole → Enter → centre 0,0.
Type AS → N (so the holes are separate circles), then I → 6 → Enter.
komandos: Specify center point of array or [Base point/Axis of rotation]:
Select grip to edit array or [ASsociative/Base point/Items/Angle between/Fill angle/ROWs/Levels/ROTate items/eXit]<eXit>:
Select grip to edit array or [ASsociative/Base point/Items/Angle between/Fill angle/ROWs/Levels/ROTate items/eXit]<eXit>:
Enter number of items in array:
Select grip to edit array or [ASsociative/Base point/Items/Angle between/Fill angle/ROWs/Levels/ROTate items/eXit]<eXit>:
uzuominos: An associative array is one object: easy to change, but the holes are no longer separate. For this lesson - AS → N.
For a rectangular grid there is ARRAYRECT: rows and columns.

ms-rotate.kodel: On a drawing the holes should sit on the centre lines - that makes dimensioning easier. ROTATE turns the selected objects around a base point.
zingsniai: ROTATE → click all 6 holes → Enter.
Base point 0,0 → angle 30.
uzuominos: A positive angle turns counter-clockwise.
After rotating, two holes lie on the horizontal axis: 35,0 and -35,0.

ms-asys.kodel: Every round part has two perpendicular centre lines through its centre - they extend 2-5 mm beyond the outline.
zingsniai: Make ASYS current.
Make KONTURAS current again.
uzuominos: The centre line looks continuous? LTSCALE → 0.5 or 1.
Centre lines are thin, so they live on their own layer ASYS.
ms-asys.tikslas: Two centre lines through the centre

testas.k: OFFSET 30 inwards from an R50 circle - what radius do you get?
testas.p: The distance is taken off the radius: 50 − 30 = 20.

testas.k: Why do we pick AS → N in ARRAYPOLAR?
v: So the holes are separate circles
testas.p: An associative array is one object, a non-associative one - separate circles.

testas.k: How do you change the layer of an object you've already drawn?
v: Only by deleting and redrawing it
Select it and pick another layer in the Layers list
testas.p: Or Ctrl+1 (Properties) → Layer.

bruksniavimas.aprasas: A bushing section: a polyline (PLINE), bore lines, ANSI31 hatching (HATCH) on layer BRUKSNIAI and a centre line.
bruksniavimas.pabaiga: You drew a hatched bushing section - this is how every hollow part is shown: pipes, bushings, housings.

bk-sluoksniai.kodel: Hatching is drawn with a thin line, so it gets its own layer. Then the lineweights print correctly.
zingsniai: NEW → acadiso.dwt.
LAYER → KONTURAS (7), ASYS (1, CENTER), MATMENYS (3) and a new BRUKSNIAI (8).
KONTURAS current.
uzuominos: Colour 8 is grey: the hatching doesn't overpower the outline.

bk-konturas.kodel: PLINE draws one connected object from several segments - it is easier to select, offset and hatch than separate LINE lines.
zingsniai: In section the ⌀20 bore shows as two lines: LINE → 0,10 → @50,0 and LINE → 0,-10 → @50,0.
uzuominos: Click the outline: if it all gets selected at once, it's a polyline.
In the section the top and bottom are walls (material), the middle is the empty bore.
bk-konturas.tikslas: A 50 × 40 outline and the bore lines

bk-hatch.kodel: In a section you hatch only where the cutting plane goes through material - the walls. The bore stays unhatched. The standard: thin lines at 45° (ANSI31).
zingsniai: Make BRUKSNIAI current.
HATCH → in the ribbon pick Pattern ANSI31, Scale 1.
Click inside the top wall, then the bottom one → Enter.
Make KONTURAS current again.
uzuominos: The whole rectangle got hatched? You clicked in the bore - U and click in the walls.
Too dense or too sparse? Select the hatch and change Scale (e.g. 0.5 or 2).

bk-asis.kodel: A turned part (bushing, shaft) always has a centre line - it extends 2-5 mm beyond the outline.
zingsniai: ASYS current: LINE → -5,0 → 55,0.
uzuominos: The centre line runs through the middle of the bore - where there's no hatching.
bk-asis.tikslas: A centre line through the bushing

testas.k: At what angle is a section hatched?
testas.p: Thin parallel lines at 45° - ANSI31.

testas.k: Which areas of a section are hatched?
v: Only where the plane cuts through material
testas.p: Holes and hollows stay unhatched.

testas.k: How is PLINE different from LINE?
testas.p: LINE creates separate segments, PLINE - one object.

sriftai.aprasas: ISO 3098 text styles: isocp.shx and ISOCPEUR with Lithuanian letters.
sriftai.pabaiga: You can create ISO text styles and write in a drawing with Lithuanian letters.

iso.kodel: Drawings use the standard engineering font (ISO 3098), not Arial.
zingsniai: Type STYLE → New → ISO:
uzuominos: Leave Height at 0 - you choose the height when writing.

isolt.kodel: isocp.shx has no ąčęėįšųūž. ISOCPEUR is the same ISO font but with Lithuanian (and other European) letters.
zingsniai: STYLE → New → ISO_LT:
uzuominos: Oblique 15° - the slanted ISO type B font.
ISOCPEUR is installed with AutoCAD - look for „isocpeur“ in the list.

tekstas.kodel: Let's check that special letters display correctly. „Brėžinys“ is Lithuanian for „drawing“. Standard heights: 2.5, 3.5, 5, 7, 10.
zingsniai: With ISO_LT current, type:
uzuominos: Question marks instead of letters? The style is not ISO_LT.
Enter twice ends TEXT.

testas.k: Why is isocp.shx not suitable for Lithuanian text?
testas.p: Use ISOCPEUR - it has the Lithuanian letters.

testas.k: Which height is NOT standard?
At what angle is the ISO type B font slanted?
testas.p: Oblique angle 15°.

matmenys.aprasas: DIMSTYLE, DIMLINEAR, DIMDIAMETER, DIMRADIUS - you will dimension the plate on layer MATMENYS (dimensions).
matmenys.pabaiga: You can create a dimension style and dimension lengths and diameters.

plokste_m.kodel: We will dimension the plate from the lesson „2D drawing“.
zingsniai: Open the drawing with the plate (OPEN) or click „Show me“ - I will draw it.
uzuominos: The plate: 100 × 60, ø30 in the centre.

dimstyle.kodel: A dimension style sets text height, arrows and gaps. The requirement is 3.5 mm text.
zingsniai: DIMSTYLE → New → name ISO_MATMENYS → Continue:
uzuominos: Set Current - so new dimensions use this style.
The text style can be ISO_LT from the lesson „Fonts and text“.

ilgis.kodel: A linear dimension is the horizontal or vertical distance between two points.
zingsniai: Make layer MATMENYS current. Type:
uzuominos: Turn on OSNAP (F3) - points will snap to corners.
For rounded corners use Endpoint on the arc ends, or type 0,0 and 100,0.

aukstis.kodel: The same DIMLINEAR - just drag the mouse sideways and the dimension becomes vertical.
zingsniai: Run DIMLINEAR again for the left edge:
uzuominos: Space repeats the last command.

skersmuo.kodel: A diameter dimension adds the ø sign automatically.
zingsniai: Type:
uzuominos: For the small holes write 4x: DIMDIAMETER → M (Mtext) → 4x<>.

spindulys.kodel: Fillets and arcs are dimensioned by their radius - an R appears before the number automatically.
zingsniai: Type:
uzuominos: Circles get a diameter (⌀), arcs and fillets - a radius (R).
Don't type over a dimension value: if it shows the wrong number, fix the drawing.

testas.k: What dimension text height is used in these drawings?
testas.p: 3.5 mm is the standard dimension text height.

testas.k: Which command dimensions a vertical length?
testas.p: DIMLINEAR - both horizontal and vertical dimensions.

testas.k: Which layer should dimensions be on?
testas.p: A separate layer - you can turn it off or change its colour.

pirmoji-3d.aprasas: BOX, CYLINDER, UNION, POLYGON, EXTRUDE, SUBTRACT, WEDGE, MIRROR3D - every command from the practical work „3D part model“.
pirmoji-3d.pabaiga: You made your first real 3D part - just like in the practical work!

pasiruosimas.kodel: AutoCAD has a separate workspace with 3D tools for modelling. The isometric view shows the part from three sides at once.
zingsniai: Open a new drawing from the acadiso.dwt template (millimetres).
Bottom right, click the gear ⚙ and choose „3D Modeling“.
At the top: View → 3D Views → SE Isometric (or a ViewCube corner).
uzuominos: The gear is called „Workspace Switching“ - it is in the status bar.
For the view you can type: -VIEW → SEISO

sluoksniai.kodel: Layers are like transparent sheets on top of each other. Outline, centre lines and dimensions have different colours and lines, so the drawing is tidy and meets the standard.
zingsniai: Type LAYER and press Enter - Layer Properties Manager opens.
With „New Layer“ create: KONTURAS (outline, colour 7 - white), ASYS (centre lines, 1 - red), MATMENYS (dimensions, 3 - green).
For layer ASYS click „Continuous“ → Load... → CENTER → OK.
Double-click KONTURAS to make it current (green tick).
uzuominos: The colour number is shown after clicking the colour square - „Color: 7“ at the bottom of the dialog.
If CENTER is not in the list - click Load..., find CENTER, select it, OK.

box.kodel: Every part starts with a main body. Starting at 0,0,0 makes all the other coordinates easy to work out.
zingsniai: Make sure layer KONTURAS is current.
Type BOX and answer the prompts in the command line:
uzuominos: Type coordinates with commas and no spaces: 100,60,0
If you click in the drawing instead of typing, the box ends up in the wrong place. Then ERASE and start again.

cylinder.kodel: The cylinder stands on top of the box, so its centre height is z = 20 - the height of the box.
zingsniai: Type CYLINDER:
uzuominos: Centre 50,30 is the middle of the box (100/2 = 50, 60/2 = 30).
Radius 20 means diameter ø40.
cylinder.tikslas: Cylinder ø40 from z=20 to z=60

union.kodel: For now these are two separate bodies. UNION turns them into one part - like gluing them.
zingsniai: Type UNION, select the box and the cylinder, press Enter.
uzuominos: After joining, hovering highlights the whole part as one object.

polygon.kodel: For the hexagonal hole we draw a hexagonal prism and later „cut“ it out. POLYGON draws a flat shape, EXTRUDE pulls it into the third dimension.
zingsniai: Draw a hexagon:
Then extrude it to a height of 60:
uzuominos: Inscribed = the hexagon's corners lie on the circle (radius 10 to a corner).
If the hexagon didn't extrude, check that you selected it in EXTRUDE, not the part.

subtract.kodel: SUBTRACT removes the second object from the first. The order matters: first WHAT FROM, then WHAT.
zingsniai: Type SUBTRACT. Select the part first (Enter), then the prism (Enter).
uzuominos: If the part disappeared and the prism is left, you swapped the order. Undo: U.
Rotate the view (Shift + middle mouse button) - you should see through the hole.
subtract.tikslas: One part with a hexagonal through-hole

wedge.kodel: The rib strengthens the joint between the cylinder and the base. WEDGE is tallest at the first corner and slopes down towards the second corner.
zingsniai: Type WEDGE:
uzuominos: The rib is 8 thick: y from 26 to 34 (30 - 4 and 30 + 4).
x = 65 - the rib goes slightly into the cylinder so they join well.

mirror.kodel: Instead of drawing the second rib again, we mirror the first one through the middle of the part. The mirror plane is YZ through x = 50.
zingsniai: Type MIRROR3D:
komandos: Specify first point of mirror plane [... YZ ...]:
uzuominos: The YZ plane is vertical and perpendicular to the X axis - exactly what we need to mirror to the left.
Answer N (No) so the original rib stays.

final.kodel: The last step is to join the ribs to the part. Then the part is ready for sheets and sections.
zingsniai: Type UNION, select everything with a window, Enter.
Look at the result: VSCURRENT → Conceptual.
uzuominos: Drag the window from left to right - it selects everything fully inside it.

testas.k: Which command cuts one body out of another?
testas.p: SUBTRACT: first select WHAT FROM, then WHAT.

testas.k: What does the POLYGON option „Inscribed in circle“ mean?
v: The polygon's corners lie on the circle
The circle touches the polygon's sides
testas.p: Inscribed: corners on the circle. Circumscribed: sides touch the circle.

testas.k: Why was the cylinder centre 50,30,20 and not 50,30,0?
v: So the cylinder stands on top of the box (box height 20)
testas.p: The third coordinate is the height Z. The top of the box is at z = 20.

testas.k: MIRROR3D asks „Delete source objects?“. What do you answer to keep both ribs?
testas.p: No - the original stays and a mirrored copy is added.

projekcijos.aprasas: European (first angle) arrangement on an A3 sheet: VIEWSTD, VIEWBASE, VIEWPROJ and an isometric view of the same model. Needs full AutoCAD.
projekcijos.pabaiga: An A3 sheet with three projections and an isometric view, all from one model. Change the model - the drawing changes too.

pr-a3.kodel: A part drawing with three projections and an isometric view needs an A3 sheet (420 × 297).
zingsniai: If you already have an A3 sheet - switch to it (tab at the bottom). You will learn the border and title block on the sheet in the last lesson.
If not - LAYOUTWIZARD: name A3, DWG To PDF.pc3, ISO full bleed A3 (420 x 297), Landscape.
uzuominos: The drawing must contain the 3D part from the lesson „First 3D part“ - we make the views from it.
To change the paper: right-click the tab → Page Setup Manager → Modify.

pr-standartas.kodel: Lithuania and Europe use first angle projection: the top view goes BELOW the front view, the left view goes on the RIGHT. The USA uses the opposite (third angle).
zingsniai: Type VIEWSTD.
Projection type: First angle. Thread style: Partial (ISO).
Click OK. Do this before placing views.
uzuominos: The first angle symbol: a truncated cone with the circles on the right.
The setting is saved in the drawing - set it again in other files (or put it in your template).

pr-priekis.kodel: The base (front) view is chosen to show the part's shape best. The other views are arranged around it.
zingsniai: On the A3 sheet type VIEWBASE → Model.
Orientation Front, scale 1:2.
Place the view top left, leaving room below and to the right. Enter, Enter.
uzuominos: To change the scale later: click the view → Scale on the ribbon.
If the view is too big - scale 1:2.5 or 1:5.
pr-priekis.tikslas: A front view on the A3 sheet

pr-projekcijos.kodel: Three views together describe the part unambiguously. They stay aligned, so dimensions can be carried across in straight lines.
zingsniai: Type VIEWPROJ and click the front view.
Move the mouse down and click - the top view.
Move the mouse to the right and click - the left view. Enter.
uzuominos: In first angle the left view is on the right - if it ended up on the left, you skipped VIEWSTD.
Views only move along their alignment - that's how it should be.

pr-aksonometrija.kodel: An isometric view helps to understand the shape quickly. It goes top right on the drawing, often with a quarter cut-out.
zingsniai: VIEWPROJ again and click the front view.
Move the mouse diagonally (up and right) and click - an isometric view appears. Enter.
Click it and choose Shaded with visible lines on the ribbon - it looks more alive.
uzuominos: Hidden lines are not shown in the isometric view.
In the lesson „Sections and quarter cut-out“ you will cut the part - the cut-out will appear in these views too.

testas.k: In first angle (European) projection the top view is...
testas.p: First angle: top view below, left view on the right.

testas.k: Which command adds projected views to an existing view?
testas.p: VIEWPROJ: select the parent view and place new ones around it.

testas.k: You changed the 3D model. What happens to the views on the sheet?
testas.p: The views are linked to the model - they update themselves or with VIEWUPDATE.

aksonometrija.aprasas: 2D isometric drafting: ISODRAFT, ISOPLANE (F5), an isometric box with polar coordinates, an isocircle (ELLIPSE → Isocircle) and a dimension with DIMEDIT Oblique.
aksonometrija.pabaiga: You can draw isometric views by hand - just like in practice task 6!

ax-isodraft.kodel: In isometric the x and y axes are rotated 30°, z is vertical. ISODRAFT changes the cursor and Ortho so lines follow these directions.
zingsniai: Open a new drawing from acadiso.dwt.
Type ISODRAFT and choose isoplaneTop (T).
F5 switches planes: Top → Right → Left. The cursor changes.
uzuominos: In older AutoCAD instead of ISODRAFT: SNAP → Style → Isometric.
The status bar has an isometric drafting button (a small cube).

ax-deze.kodel: In isometric, sizes are measured true length along the axes - 30°, 150° and vertically. Polar coordinates @length<angle do this exactly.
zingsniai: Type LINE and enter the points in order - one line goes round the bottom and the front edges.
A second LINE draws the last top edge.
uzuominos: @60<30 means: 60 mm at 30° from the last point.
Made a mistake? U (Undo) inside LINE undoes only the last point.

ax-apskritimas.kodel: A circle in isometric is seen as an ellipse. The ELLIPSE Isocircle option draws it exactly in the current plane.
zingsniai: Press F5 until the command line shows <Isoplane Top>.
ELLIPSE → I (Isocircle). Centre - the middle of the top face, radius 10.
uzuominos: The Isocircle option appears only when isometric drafting is on (step 1).
Find the centre without numbers: Shift + right-click → Mid Between 2 Points → two opposite top corners.

ax-matmuo.kodel: In isometric a dimension is placed parallel to the edge, and the extension lines are turned along an axis - otherwise the dimension „falls out“ of the plane.
zingsniai: DIMALIGNED: click both ends of the bottom right edge (60 mm) and place the dimension below.
DIMEDIT → Oblique: select the dimension and type 90 - the extension lines become vertical.
uzuominos: Pick the ends with OSNAP Endpoint - then the dimension is exactly 60.
Isometric dimension text often uses a text style slanted ±30°.

testas.k: At what angle are the x and y axes drawn in isometric?
testas.p: In isometric x and y are at 30° to the horizontal, z is vertical.

testas.k: How is a circle shown in isometric?
testas.p: A circle in isometric is seen as an ellipse - ELLIPSE → Isocircle.

testas.k: Which key switches the isometric plane (Top/Right/Left)?
testas.p: F5 (or Ctrl+E) switches the isoplane.

pjuviai.aprasas: A quarter cut-out in the 3D part, SECTIONPLANE, VIEWBASE and VIEWSECTION - section A–A on a sheet. Needs full AutoCAD (Model Documentation).
pjuviai.pabaiga: Your part has a quarter cut-out and the sheet has section A–A - this is how real drawings show the inside of a part.

pj-detale.kodel: Sections are made from a finished model. We use the part from the lesson „First 3D part“: 100 × 60 × 60 with a hexagonal hole.
zingsniai: Open the drawing with the part from the lesson „First 3D part“ (if you no longer have it, click „Show me“ and I will draw it).
Switch to the 3D Modeling workspace and the SE Isometric view.
The part must be a single body - if not, UNION.
uzuominos: One body: clicking anywhere on the part selects the whole part.
If the part is made of several pieces - UNION, select everything, Enter.

pj-ispjova.kodel: A quarter cut-out removes a quarter of the part so the inside is visible: the hole and the wall thickness. In an isometric view it replaces a separate section.
zingsniai: Draw a box covering the front right quarter - from the middle of the part to the corner, through the full height.
SUBTRACT: select the part first (WHAT FROM), Enter, then the box (WHAT), Enter.
uzuominos: The quarter starts in the middle of the part: x = 50 (half of 100), y = 30 (half of 60).
Cut the wrong quarter? U undoes it - try again.
pj-ispjova.tikslas: The hexagonal hole is visible, volume ~118 927 mm³

pj-plokstuma.kodel: A section plane is like a knife: it shows where the part is cut. AutoCAD shows the section both in 3D and on the sheet.
zingsniai: Type SECTIONPLANE.
Choose Orthographic (O) and Front - the plane goes through the middle of the part, parallel to the front.
Click the plane and drag the arrow - watch the section change.
uzuominos: The plane looks like a transparent rectangle with an arrow - the arrow shows the viewing direction.
Live section: click the plane → right-click → Activate live sectioning.
pj-plokstuma.tikslas: A section plane through the part

pj-vaizdas.pavadinimas: Base view on a sheet: VIEWBASE
pj-vaizdas.kodel: You already know VIEWBASE from the lesson „Projections from a 3D model“: it draws 2D views on a sheet from the 3D model. Dimensions always match the model, and the views update when the model changes.
zingsniai: Click the Layout1 tab at the bottom.
Type VIEWBASE, choose Model, orientation Front and scale 1:2.
Place the view top left and press Enter. Don't add projected views yet - press Enter again.
uzuominos: AutoCAD says „Unknown command VIEWBASE“? Your AutoCAD has no Model Documentation (e.g. AutoCAD LT) - you can skip this and the next two steps.
To move a view: click it and drag the blue square.
pj-vaizdas.tikslas: A front view on the sheet

pj-pjuvis.kodel: A section shows the inside of the part as if it were cut. The cut is marked by a line with the letters A–A, and the cut material is hatched.
zingsniai: Type VIEWSECTION and click the base view.
Type Full. Click two points across the middle of the view - start and end outside the part.
Press Enter and place the section below the view.
uzuominos: Pick the middle with OSNAP Midpoint, then move the mouse sideways and click outside the part.
The letters A–A are added automatically. To change them, click the section line.
pj-pjuvis.tikslas: Section A–A with hatching on the sheet

testas.k: Which command creates a 2D view on a sheet from a 3D model?
testas.p: VIEWBASE creates the base view; projected views and sections are made from it.

testas.k: For a quarter cut-out a box is removed from the part. Which command?
testas.p: SUBTRACT: first WHAT FROM (the part), then WHAT (the box).

testas.k: How is cut metal shown in a section?
testas.p: Metal is hatched with thin parallel lines at 45° (ANSI31).

schema.aprasas: A symbol, attributes (ATTDEF), a block (BLOCK), inserting (INSERT) and a parts list (DATAEXTRACTION).
schema.pabaiga: You can create blocks with attributes and build a parts list - the basis of diagram work.

naujas_sch.kodel: We draw the diagram in a clean drawing so it doesn't mix with the plate.
zingsniai: Create a new drawing from acadiso.dwt (as in the lesson „File and formats“).
uzuominos: Ctrl+N - a quick new drawing.

zenklas.kodel: All diagram symbols have the same length - 20 mm. Resistor: a 10 × 4 rectangle and two leads.
zingsniai: Draw:
uzuominos: The symbol is 20 long: 5 + 10 + 5.

attdef.kodel: An attribute is a field inside a block. POZ (R1, R2...) is visible on the diagram, NUORODA (1 kΩ) is invisible but goes into the parts list.
zingsniai: Run ATTDEF twice:
komandos: Tag: POZ · Prompt: Reference designator · Default: R · point 7,4
uzuominos: The tag becomes the column name in the parts list. Keep the tags POZ and NUORODA - Brėžly checks them.
The Invisible tick box is on the left of the dialog (Mode).

block.kodel: A block is a symbol you draw once and insert as many times as you like. Change the block and all copies change.
zingsniai: Type BLOCK:
uzuominos: Base point 0,0 is the left lead - you will „drag“ the block by it.
Delete - the symbol disappears but the block stays in memory.

insert.kodel: Every time you insert the block, AutoCAD asks for the attribute values.
zingsniai: INSERT → REZISTORIUS → place it 3 times:
uzuominos: If it doesn't ask for attributes - ATTREQ → 1.
Fix a wrong value by double-clicking the block.

lentele.kodel: The parts list is built automatically from the block attributes - nothing to retype by hand.
zingsniai: Type DATAEXTRACTION and go through the wizard:
uzuominos: The Count column shows how many of each part there are.
Place the table next to the diagram.

testas.k: Why is the NUORODA (value) attribute set to Invisible?
v: So it takes no space on the diagram but is in the table
testas.p: Invisible on the diagram, but DATAEXTRACTION puts it into the parts list.

testas.k: What does the Delete option of BLOCK do?
v: Deletes the original objects, the block stays in memory
testas.p: The objects disappear from the drawing, the block stays - you insert it with INSERT.

testas.k: How long are the diagram symbols in this lesson?
testas.p: Equal length makes the wires easy to connect.

lapas.pavadinimas: A3 sheet: border and title block
lapas.aprasas: The last lesson: an A3 sheet (LAYOUTWIZARD), the border and your title block in its corner - this is how a finished drawing looks.
lapas.pabaiga: You finished all the lessons! You can prepare an A3 sheet with a border and a title block - every drawing is handed in like this.

a3.kodel: In Model space you draw at real size, while the sheet (Layout / PAPER) is the paper you will print. A3 = 420 × 297 mm.
zingsniai: Type LAYOUTWIZARD and go through the pages:
uzuominos: A tab called „A3“ appears at the bottom - that is your sheet.
If A3 is not in the paper list, first choose the DWG To PDF printer.

remelis.kodel: By the standard the border is 20 mm from the left edge (for binding) and 5 mm on the other sides.
zingsniai: On the A3 sheet (not Model!), on layer KONTURAS (outline), type:
uzuominos: Check that the A3 tab is active at the bottom, not Model.

kampinis.pavadinimas: Title block onto the sheet: COPYBASE
kampinis.kodel: You already drew the title block in the lesson „Title block“. Its coordinates (230,5 - 415,45) match the corner of the sheet, so once copied it lands exactly where it belongs.
zingsniai: Open Title_block.dwg, type COPYBASE, base point 0,0, select the table with its texts and press Enter.
Go back to this drawing and, on the A3 sheet, paste:
uzuominos: Ctrl+Shift+C is the same as COPYBASE, Ctrl+V is PASTECLIP.
Don't have the file any more? Draw the table right here on the sheet: RECTANG → 230,5 → 415,45 and the inner lines, as in the lesson „Title block“.
kampinis.tikslas: A 185 × 40 table in the sheet corner

uzpildyk.kodel: An empty title block is the first thing your tutor will notice.
zingsniai: If you copied it with texts, they are already there: double-click the title and change it to this drawing's title.
If there are no texts - type the drawing title (height 5) and your name (height 2.5).
uzuominos: Double-clicked text can be edited in place.
Enter twice ends the TEXT command.
You can move text with MOVE.
uzpildyk.tikslas: At least 2 texts in the table

testas.k: How far is the border from the left edge of the sheet?
testas.p: 20 mm on the left for binding, 5 mm elsewhere.

testas.k: Where does the title block go?
testas.p: Always in the bottom right corner of the border.

testas.k: What size is an A3 sheet?

patarimai: In AutoCAD the Space bar works like Enter - and an empty Space repeats the last command.
Esc cancels any command. Stuck? Press Esc twice.
U undoes the last action. Your best friend while learning!
F8 turns on ORTHO - lines only horizontal and vertical.
Shift + middle mouse button rotates the 3D view (orbit).
Double-click the mouse wheel - ZOOM Extents: shows the whole drawing.
The first letters are enough in the command line: L = LINE, C = CIRCLE, EXT = EXTRUDE.
VSCURRENT → C (Conceptual) shows the part in colour and nicely lit.
Never draw on layer 0 - it's meant for blocks. And put nothing on Defpoints: that layer doesn't print.
Draw 1:1 in real millimetres. The scale is set only on the layout, when printing.
Don't type over a dimension value: if it shows the wrong number, the drawing is inaccurate - fix the drawing.
Don't EXPLODE dimensions and blocks - they lose their properties and are hard to fix.
Ctrl+S - often! AutoCAD sometimes freezes, and unsaved work is lost.
A box from left to right selects only what fits inside it completely; from right to left - everything it touches.

NEW.ka: A new drawing from a template. For our drawings - acadiso.dwt (millimetres).

SAVEAS.ka: Saves the drawing under a new name or in another format (DWG, DXF, older version).

PLOT.ka: Prints. With DWG To PDF.pc3 it creates a PDF file.

LAYOUTWIZARD.ka: Wizard for a new sheet (Layout): printer, paper, orientation.

RECTANG.ka: A rectangle from two opposite corners.

LAYER.ka: Layer management: outline, centre lines, dimensions - different lines and colours.

LINE.ka: A line segment between points. Enter ends it.

CIRCLE.ka: A circle: centre and radius (D - diameter).

FILLET.ka: Rounds a corner. P (Polyline) - all corners of a polyline.

COPY.ka: Copies objects from one point to another.
COPY.pvz: COPY → object → base point → new point

ATTDEF.ka: Attribute definition - a field in a block (e.g. POZ, NUORODA).

BLOCK.ka: Creates a block from objects - a symbol you can insert many times.

INSERT.ka: Inserts a block and asks for the attribute values.

DATAEXTRACTION.ka: Extracts block attributes into a table - the parts list.

DIMSTYLE.ka: Dimension style: text height, arrows, precision.

DIMLINEAR.ka: A horizontal or vertical linear dimension.

DIMDIAMETER.ka: A diameter dimension with the ø sign.

STYLE.ka: Text style: font (isocp.shx, ISOCPEUR), oblique angle.

CYLINDER.ka: A 3D cylinder: base centre, radius, height.

SUBTRACT.ka: Removes one body from another (holes, grooves).
SUBTRACT.pvz: SUBTRACT → from what → what to remove

EXTRUDE.ka: Pulls a 2D profile into a 3D body.

MIRROR3D.ka: A mirror copy in 3D space across a plane.

SECTIONPLANE.ka: A section plane through a 3D model; live section shows the inside.

VIEWBASE.ka: Creates a 2D view on a sheet from a 3D model (Model Documentation).

VIEWSECTION.ka: A section from a view on the sheet: Full, Half, Offset, Aligned.

VIEWSTD.ka: Drawing view standard: projection arrangement (First angle - Europe).

VIEWPROJ.ka: Adds projected and isometric views to an existing view.

ISODRAFT.ka: Isometric drafting: cursor and Ortho along the 30° axes.

ELLIPSE.ka: An ellipse; in isometric the Isocircle option draws an isocircle.

DIMEDIT.ka: Edits dimensions; Oblique turns the extension lines.

ZOOM.ka: Zooms in and out. E (Extents) shows the whole drawing - so does double-clicking the wheel.

OSNAP.ka: Object snap settings: Endpoint, Midpoint, Center... F3 - turn on and off.

AREA.ka: Measures the area and perimeter of the points you click.

DIST.ka: Measures the distance and angle between two points.

MOVE.ka: Moves objects: base point → new place.

CHAMFER.ka: Chamfers a corner. D (Distance) - the distances, P (Polyline) - all corners.

TRIM.ka: Cuts off part of an object up to other objects. With Shift - extends (EXTEND).
TRIM.pvz: TRIM → click what to cut off → Enter

EXTEND.ka: Extends a line to another object (a boundary).
EXTEND.pvz: EXTEND → click the end of the line → Enter

MIRROR.ka: A mirror copy across a line. N - keep the original.
MIRROR.pvz: MIRROR → objects → 2 points of the line → N

OFFSET.ka: A parallel copy at a given distance: for a line, circle, polyline.

ARRAYPOLAR.ka: Copies spaced evenly around a centre (polar array).

ARRAYRECT.ka: Copies in rows and columns (rectangular array).

ROTATE.ka: Rotates objects around a base point.

MATCHPROP.ka: Copies the layer and properties from one object to others.

PLINE.ka: A polyline - one object made of segments and arcs.

HATCH.ka: Hatches a closed area. For sections - ANSI31.

DIMRADIUS.ka: A radius dimension - R before the number.
